system_description.narrative_title: Middle East conflict fuels oil & shipping crisis
system_description.narrative_summary: Escalating hostilities around the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz — driven by Houthi attacks, Iranian-linked operations and regional military responses — are disrupting tanker routes and oil logistics, thinning global fuel buffers and causing pronounced market volatility. As an open system this involves flows (oil, ships, information), inputs (attacks, production changes, inventories, policy actions), outputs (prices, rerouting, stock releases, military deployments) and feedbacks (attacks → reduced flows → price spikes → policy/market responses → altered incentives for further attacks or protection). Governments, oil companies, traders and shipping insurers are responding with stock releases, pricing moves and enhanced security, but executives warn logistics constraints and tanker shortages could keep markets unsettled for months or years.
system_description.scope: Maritime chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Bab el‑Mandeb), Middle East oil producers and export infrastructure, tanker fleet and shipping logistics, global crude and refined product inventories/markets, regional security actors and military responses, insurance and charter markets.
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil trading, storage and insurance markets
Regional military alliances and security architecture
Refining, inland fuel distribution and diesel markets

variables.name: Transit flow through maritime chokepoints
variables.description: Measures the volumetric rate of oil and oil-bearing vessels transiting key maritime chokepoints per unit time.

variables.name: Crude oil production rate
variables.description: Measures the rate of crude oil production available for export from regional producers per unit time.

variables.name: Refined product output rate
variables.description: Measures the rate at which refined fuels and diesel are produced and dispatched from refineries per unit time.

variables.name: Global oil inventory level
variables.description: Measures the total volume of crude and refined product stocks held in commercial and strategic reserves available to markets.

variables.name: Fuel buffer thickness
variables.description: Measures the readily deployable cushion of refined fuel relative to typical consumption (e.g., days of cover).

variables.name: Tanker fleet availability
variables.description: Measures the number and carrying capacity of tankers available and ready for charter to move oil.

variables.name: Tanker utilization rate
variables.description: Proportion of the existing tanker fleet currently engaged in voyages or under contract versus idle.

variables.name: Shipping routing flexibility
variables.description: Measures the capacity to reroute maritime shipments to alternative routes (longer distance or different corridors) without losing throughput.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: Average cost level of insurance coverage for tanker voyages through higher-risk maritime areas, reflecting perceived risk and underwriting capacity.

variables.name: Maritime freight rate index
variables.description: Measures average charter and freight costs for oil tankers across routes relevant to the system.

variables.name: Maritime security incident rate
variables.description: Frequency of hostile incidents (attacks, seizures, strikes) against commercial shipping in the region per unit time.

variables.name: Military protection deployment level
variables.description: Scale and intensity of military escorts, patrols and protective measures active in maritime areas affecting commercial shipping.

variables.name: Export infrastructure throughput capacity
variables.description: Maximum sustainable flow capacity of ports, pipelines and terminals for oil and refined product exports.

variables.name: Oil market price level
variables.description: Spot price level of benchmark crude and major refined products reflecting current market valuation.

variables.name: Price volatility
variables.description: Short‑term variability of oil and refined fuel prices measured by statistical dispersion or realized volatility.

variables.name: Logistics bottleneck severity
variables.description: Degree to which logistics constraints (crew availability, port congestion, tanker shortages, transit delays) reduce effective transport capacity.

catalysts.title: Coordinated diesel/crude stock releases by IEA/G7
catalysts.description: Planned coordinated releases of diesel (and some crude) by IEA/G7 members to calm markets and replace thinning fuel buffers.
catalysts.rationale: IEA to meet and members agree to prioritise diesel release; G7 plans crude/diesel releases (IEA/G7 headlines, 2026-10-07/10-08).

catalysts.title: Escalation in Houthi / Iranian-linked attacks on shipping
catalysts.description: Ongoing surge of missile, drone and tanker attacks in Red Sea/Strait of Hormuz that raises risks to commercial shipping and transits.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines report record attacks on tankers, stepped-up Iranian/Houthi strikes, and renewed missile/drone strikes on ports (10-06 to 10-08).

catalysts.title: Sustained Gulf export recovery via pipelines/terminals
catalysts.description: Continued recovery of Middle East exports toward pre-war levels driven by pipeline rerouting and terminal throughput rather than secure chokepoint transits alone.
catalysts.rationale: Reports show Gulf flows averaged ~81% of pre-war, East‑West pipeline pumping 5.8m bpd and exports topping pre-war levels for parts of September (10-06/10-07).

catalysts.title: Tropical cyclone threat to U.S. Gulf oil & refining
catalysts.description: Forecasted tropical storm/hurricane threat to the U.S. Gulf Coast that could disrupt production, refining and port operations in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Forecast: Tropical Storm Isaias expected to hit US Gulf coast as a hurricane early Saturday (10-08 headline).

catalysts.title: Surge in private tanker charters, purchases and storage trades
catalysts.description: Traders and firms are accelerating tanker charters and purchases to store cargoes or avoid risky routes, tightening spot tanker availability and raising freight/insurance premiums.
catalysts.rationale: Coverage: US trader takes $2bn tanker bet; Vitol warns of tanker shortage; SFL selling tankers to Trafigura (10-07/10-06).

catalysts.title: Mutual defence pact and allied maritime protection deployments
catalysts.description: New mutual-defence arrangements and allied technical/defensive support prompt increased naval patrols and escorts in maritime approaches influencing shipping security.
catalysts.rationale: Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey mutual defence pact and Turkey sending defensive support to Saudi Arabia (10-06/10-07 headlines).

catalysts.title: Iran threatens to block 'illegal' Strait of Hormuz routes
catalysts.description: Official Iranian statements to block so-called 'illegal' routes in the Strait could restrict navigation lanes and raise transit risk and costs if enforced.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Iranian official says 'illegal routes' in Strait of Hormuz to soon be blocked (10-07), raising transit vulnerability.
